text:
ana: Heads-up — saw a spike in token/retry cost overnight from a small set of long-running streaming calls. Suspect routing slice sharding + failover duplicated work. Anyone seen this pattern?

chris: Yup, noticed similar in the dashboards. A handful of streams retried to different upstreams while KV cache warmed, so we ended up re-generating ~2x tokens for same requests.

mira: Do you have an example trace? Is it hedging or straight failover? :thinking_face:

ana: (typo) ana: Traces attached — I'll paste a short snippet of the span chain. Looks like: frontdoor -> slice-A -> client disconnect -> frontdoor retries -> slice-B warmup -> resumed stream but without cached prefix.

jordan: That's the classic cold-KV + multi-slice failover case. We currently roll retries to any healthy slice; we lose prefix cache affinity so retry does more work.

chris: Two quick ideas: 1) make retries prefer same slice within short window (sticky retry) 2) add retry-cost tags to telemetry so billing/alerts can separate retries from original tokens.

mira: I like 1 but worry about single-slice overload if that slice is flapping. Maybe a conditional sticky policy: stick if slice has healthy warmup flag AND retry_count < 1.

ana: Agreed. Also want to preserve stream continuity for user-facing sessions — if we do sticky but slice dead, fallback should be graceful with an explicit resumable-token handshake.

jordan: Sketch of policy (very rough):
```yaml
retry_policy:
  prefer_same_slice: true
  prefer_window_secs: 10
  allow_fallback: true
  fallback_behavior:
    type: resumable_handoff
    token_header: X-Resume-Token
```

mira: Nice. We need telemetry fields: retry_reason, retry_target_slice, retry_was_sticky (bool), tokens_accounted_for_retry. That lets Optimize/finance pinpoint costs.

chris: Also add a metric for "replay_tokens" vs "user_tokens" at per-request granularity so we can attribute unit cost.

ana: Ops question — how does this interact with our current admission/hedging logic? If we bias retries to same slice, do we reduce hedging effectiveness for high-priority clients?

jordan: Hedging stays but hedges should be aware of sticky preference. i.e., hedges can still go to other slices, but primary retry attempt prefers original. Hedging remains as a last resort after prefer_window expires.

mira: Implementation notes: small runtime change in frontdoor route selection, a runtime flag to enable conditional stickiness, and a short-lived KV warmup signal we propagate to the control-plane.

ana: Who wants to own a tiny RFC? I'll volunteer to draft if someone can sign off on telemetry fields.

chris: I'll take telemetry sign-off and add the metrics to the ingestion spec.

jordan: I'll review the RFC from an admission/hedging POV.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: FYI — deploy 2026-03-22T02:14:30Z touched frontdoor routing code (PR #4012). Could be related.

mira: Good call — ana can you correlate the spike to that deploy? If so we may want a rollback/patch.

ana: Will check and post a short follow-up with timestamps. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
